name: GitHub Actions Runner
description: GitHub Actions Runner is the agent that executes self-hosted jobs. One Debian container registers several runner processes per repository, so a personal account can run concurrent jobs without sharing one registration across repos.

app_vars.name: var_gh_owner
app_vars.label: GitHub owner
app_vars.help: User or organization that owns the repositories. A repository in var_gh_repos may also be written as owner/repo.

app_vars.name: var_gh_repos
app_vars.label: Repositories
app_vars.help: Comma-separated repository names, or owner/repo when a repo belongs to another account.

app_vars.name: var_gh_token
app_vars.label: GitHub token
app_vars.help: Classic PAT with the repo scope, or a fine-grained token with Administration read and write on each repository. Used to mint registration tokens and then discarded.

app_vars.name: var_runner_count
app_vars.label: Runners per repository
app_vars.help: How many runner processes to register for each repository. A runner executes one job at a time.

app_vars.name: var_runner_name
app_vars.label: Runner name prefix
app_vars.help: GitHub shows each process as <prefix>-1, <prefix>-2, and so on.

notes.text: Debian 13 only. Defaults are 4 cores, 12 GB RAM, and 40 GB disk because a single job such as govulncheck can use several gigabytes.
Docker is installed so workflow jobs can run containers. The runner itself is installed from the upstream tarball. Nested virtualization has to stay enabled.
The service runs as root with RUNNER_ALLOW_RUNASROOT=1. Workflow code from the registered repositories has root inside this container.
Every job on this container shares one network namespace. Two jobs that publish the same host port, such as Postgres on 5432, will attach to each other's services.
The GitHub token is not written to disk. Updates replace the binaries under /opt/actions-runner and copy them onto the existing registrations. They do not ask for the token again.
